subject: Validation sprint: dedicated fleet throttle windows & handoff cadence
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2026 14:05:00 +0000
Subject: Validation sprint proposal for StrataCorp (hosted -> dedicated)

Team —

Summary: StrataCorp (DEAL-4891) is ready to commit to a Dedicated pool but needs an engineering-validated sizing run and an operational handoff cadence that preserves the existing SLA (99.95% availability, p95 < 250ms for gen endpoints). They want a two-week validation sprint followed by a single-day canary swap and a business-window full cutover.

Proposed high-level plan (this is what I shared with the customer):
- Week 1 (staging validation): mirror 30% of production traffic to dedicated staging pool; run evening peak replay and targeted load tests.
- Week 2 (stress and regression): ramp to 70% of observed 99th percentile QPS for 4x sustained bursts; validate batching, KV-cache warmup behavior, and p95.
- Canary day: a 4-hour canary where 10% of live traffic routes to Dedicated with automatic fallback to Hosted on errors.
- Cutover window: 02:00–05:00 UTC on a mutually agreed date (business prefers 03:00 UTC).

Key sizing targets (from the attached calc and load test):
- Target sustained QPS: 6.2k token-requests/sec (sampled; see CSV).
- Working baseline: 48 T4v4-equivalent GPUs (est. after model perf adjustments & 4-way quantization); target headroom: +30% for burst absorption.
- Accept criteria: sustained p95 <= 260ms on canary, error rate <= 0.5% and no more than one rollback-triggering incident.

Asks for ops/infra:
1) Ben/Karthik: confirm GPU type equivalence (T4v4 vs A100 batch tradeoffs) and whether autoscale boundaries need explicit pre-warming.
2) Marissa: coordinate SRE calendar and on-call coverage for the canary and cutover windows (need 2 SREs + 1 on-call TL).
3) Team: review attached load-test CSV + capacity_calc_v2 and prepare a staging playbook (I attached a draft migration_canary_playbook.md).

I want a short runbook we can give StrataCorp that includes throttle/slow-start policies and the automatic fallback thresholds (errors, p95 spike, and tail-latency). I'll consolidate responses into a single validation checklist by Mon.

Thanks —
Mina
Mina Haddad
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina.haddad@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0193

Attachments: stratacorp-load-test-results-20261210.csv (summary rows), capacity_calc_v2.xlsx, migration_canary_playbook.md

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Validation sprint proposal for StrataCorp (hosted -> dedicated)

Thanks, Mina — good concise plan. A couple of clarifying items from infra perspective:

1) GPU mapping: the "48 T4v4-equivalent" number in the spreadsheet assumes a batch size of 32 and persistent KV-cache hot paths for chat workloads. If StrataCorp's sessions are short-turning (avg tokens per req > 1k), we should either increase card count or reduce batch to keep p95 under target.

2) Autoscale pre-warm: we should implement a staged pre-warm during canary day: 25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100% over 90 minutes to avoid cold-start spikes on model kernel selection. This requires reserved capacity lease on the Dedicated fleet for the canary window.

3) Fallback & throttles: I'll draft two throttle policies: (A) soft throttle (qps cap per route with 10s leaky-bucket smoothing) and (B) hard cutoff (risk-managed fallback to Hosted). The canary playbook should call these out with exact thresholds.

Action items assigned:
- Ben: produce throttle.json snippet + recommended pre-warm ramp (by Wed EOD).
- Karthik: confirm latency delta for A100 (if customer can choose) vs our T4 baseline; specifically want expected p95 delta at batch=32.
- Marissa: publish SRE shift for Dec 28 canary; confirm 2 SREs + TL availability.

Ben
Ben Carter
Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

From: Alex Garcia <alex.garcia@stratacorp.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Cc: Emma Li <emma.li@stratacorp.com>, contracts@stratacorp.com
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2026 18:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Validation sprint proposal for StrataCorp (hosted -> dedicated)

Mina — thanks for the plan. A few notes from our side to align on business constraints:

- Timeline: StrataCorp wants staging validation completed by Jan 8 so procurement can finalize the PO by Jan 12. That means we need the canary on the last week of Dec or the first week of Jan.
- Audit/retention: We require 13 months of request-level audit logs and a signed SLA addendum covering a 99.95% uptime objective on the Dedicated pool. Please include the audit log retention plan in the playbook.
- Acceptance criteria: we need a quantitative rollback policy documented (e.g., rollback if p95 crosses 350ms for >15m or error rate >1% for >10m). The thresholds you proposed are reasonable but we require explicit time windows and on-call escalation contact.

We can do a canary on Dec 28 (03:00 UTC) if Redwood provides the pre-warm window and the fallback automation. Contracts is looped to start the PO and SLA addendum redline. Emma will coordinate internal SRE coverage.

Alex Garcia
Head of Platform Engineering, StrataCorp
alex.garcia@stratacorp.com

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 18 Dec 2026 16:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Validation sprint proposal for StrataCorp (hosted -> dedicated)

Looping up final technical plan and runbook updates. Draft summary of the operational playbook items we will deliver (attached as migration_canary_playbook.md):

- Pre-warm sequence: reserve 40 GPUs (warm to 25%, 50%, 75%, 100% over 90 minutes). Metrics gating at each step (p95, CPU steal, model kernel OOM rate).
- Canary traffic routing: 10% traffic split implemented via smart-router with a 1min reconcile period and automatic rollback hook on threshold breaches.
- Throttle policy (soft): per-route QPS caps based on token-rate; soft throttle emits 429s with header X-Redwood-Throttle=soft and retries advised.
- Throttle policy (hard): if error rate > 0.8% for 5 consecutive minutes OR p95 > 320ms for 10 minutes, trigger immediate full-fallback to Hosted and notify both on-call and customer channels.
- Observability: pre-signed Drive folder with dashboards (links above); we will enable request-level audit logs for 13 months per StrataCorp's ask; logs will be stored in their dedicated S3 bucket (contract to confirm storage SLA).
- Rollback play: automated rollback (traffic reconciling back to Hosted) + postmortem timeline (15min triage, 60min mitigation window, follow-up RCA within 72 hours).

Attachments included: migration_canary_playbook.md (detailed steps), capacity_calc_v2.xlsx (finalized numbers), stratacorp-load-test-results-20261210.csv (test outputs).

Marissa — per Ben's ask, please confirm SRE coverage and share the zoom link for the canary ops room. Once you confirm, I'll add the exact pre-warm API calls to the playbook and we can publish the single-page acceptance checklist we hand to the customer.

Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
